prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Regional Dispatch Center (Juniper) coordinates incidents, dispatch, jurisdictional coverage, shared records, surge and mutual aid; jurisdictions retain resource ownership/local-policy responsibility. Call Taker Mara (Larkspur) confirms/repeats location, gathers callback/clinical/access details, preserves original reports and separates facts from estimates; produces Caller Location Correction Slip, receives Bedside Arrival Receipt and verifies arrival time. Keep caller connected when feasible during alternate-channel crew contact. Triage Supervisor (Copperfield) resolves uncertainty, records priority/rationale/response level, sends Pediatric Acuity Note, validates surge and approves/documents temporary overrides before use; flags calls needing immediate radio access, reviews suspected-duplicate audit memos and cases where acuity/escalation timing may affect patient risk. Regional Medical Director sets clinical policy/priorities, advises specialty care/destinations and communications-constrained prioritization, reviews findings and approves regional-scope guidance changes; no dispatch authority. Shift Commander (Sundial) manages readiness/surge/coverage, reviews coverage before moves, approves material coverage-reducing exceptions, sends Mutual Aid Release Form, receives Coverage Gap Bulletin, adjusts staffing/deployment and may restrict capability for unacceptable unresolved risk; records restriction rationale, scope and duration. Authority transfers only on successor acknowledgment or higher command; outgoing records incidents, failures, temporary channels and pending decisions; incoming verifies assignments/paths. Paramedic Crew reports readiness/status, position, changes/hazards; stages until relocation/direct assignment confirmed, reassesses pediatric patients en route, reports material changes, follows safety procedures and avoids uncertain areas without confirmed instructions. Ambulance Unit 417 reports arrival/handover, last confirmed position and safe status after contact returns; reassignment requires dispatch confirmation obligations permit. Radio Coordinator (Mistral) manages Regional Radio Network reachability, backups, assignments, priorities/routes and Coverage Gap Bulletin; records channel changes/effective times on change card and uses South Access Lane Notice in operational review. Failed voice contact: approved data channel if available; timestamp attempts. Crews acknowledge/repeat critical location, priority/destination; correct discrepancies; handoffs require acknowledgment/dispatch confirmation. Degraded-radio mode prioritizes emergency traffic/common picture; announce outages, affected areas/restoration; fallback movement requires acknowledgment/repetition. CAD Console (Computer Aided Dispatch Console) shows latest confirmed unit status, time/source. Ambulance Coordination Platform timestamps/queues updates through brief interruptions, flags reconciliation and distinguishes accepted mutual-aid resources from local units. Coverage checks compare successful radio checks with planned intervals. North/South

New part:
S247: The Regional Dispatch Center provides a periodic summary of assurance activities, open risks, and improvement progress to regional oversight.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
